LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING – LETTER OF REQUEST

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we need to make formal requests for membership to groups and institutions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication
2. appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING – LETTER OF REQUEST
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING – LETTER OF REQUEST
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we need to make formal requests for membership to groups and institutions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing – Letter of request means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: compose a letter of request (for library or club membership) for effective communication.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of letter writing for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
